P·01  ·  AGRICULTURE  ·  ON THE VF BUILD SLATE

Field IntelligenceThe agronomist every farm can afford to consult.

The precision-agriculture industry built its tools for estates measured in thousands of hectares. Field Intelligence takes the same class of crop-health, irrigation and yield analysis and scales it down to the small farms that feed Europe.

WHY IT HAS TO EXIST

Precision farming exists.
Small farms were priced out of it.

The technology gap in agriculture is about who gets access. The numbers are stark: the larger the farm, the more likely it already runs on data. The smaller the farm, the more likely it runs on memory and hope.

F·01

Adoption follows farm size

US Department of Agriculture data shows around 73% of large crop farms use guidance and precision systems, against roughly 10% of small ones. Yield-mapping adoption shows the same cliff: about 68% on large operations, 13% on small. The tools exist; vendors packaged them for the large end only.

F·02

Europe farms small

Eurostat counts 62.8% of all EU farms at under five hectares. In Malta it is 97%. The overwhelming majority of European agriculture operates at the scale the precision-farming industry treats as an afterthought.

F·03

Consultancy does not scale down

An agronomist on retainer, soil labs, scouting programmes: the advisory layer that big estates buy is priced per visit and per hectare, which makes no sense at three hectares of vines or vegetables.

F·04

The data is already overhead

Sentinel satellites pass over every European field every few days, free of charge. Weather models cover every parish. The missing piece is a system that turns that data into one clear instruction a working farmer can act on.

Built for the farms
statistics call small.

The Mediterranean smallholding

VF designs Field Intelligence from Gozo outward: terraced plots, mixed crops, scarce water, no data team. If the system earns its keep on a Maltese smallholding, the EU’s smallest-farm landscape, it will earn it anywhere.

TERRACED PLOTSMIXED CROPPINGWATER-SCARCENO DATA TEAM

Family farms

Operations run by one household, where every hour in front of a dashboard is an hour not spent in the field. The system answers questions; it does not create a new job.

Part-time growers

A huge share of European holdings are farmed alongside other work. Field Intelligence watches the fields on the days the farmer cannot.

Small cooperatives

Groups of growers who share machinery and markets can share field intelligence the same way: one system, many plots, each member seeing their own land.

Agronomists and advisors

A multiplier for agronomy. Advisors serve more farms when the routine watching is already done and only the judgement calls remain.

WHAT IT CHANGES

From satellite pass
to one clear instruction.

The measure of the system is whether a farmer standing in a field with wet boots and a phone gets an answer worth acting on.

See stress before it spreads.

Vegetation indices from every satellite pass, compared against the field’s own history, with anomalies flagged in plain language instead of colour maps the farmer has to decode.

Water on evidence.

Irrigation guidance built from weather, soil class and observed canopy response, pointed at the Mediterranean reality of scarce, expensive water.

Know the season early.

Yield outlooks that sharpen as the season runs, so you make selling, storage and labour decisions on the best available signal rather than last year’s memory.

THE MECHANICS

Free data in,
judgement out.

The architecture is humble by design: public satellite and weather data at the bottom, careful agronomic modelling in the middle, and a farmer-grade interface on top. No proprietary sensors required to start.

Every VF system runs on the harness stack, is steered by the Helmsman engine and is watched from a command dashboard.

LAYER 1

The observation layer

Sentinel-2 imagery and regional weather models, ingested continuously per registered field boundary. This layer costs the farmer nothing: it is European public infrastructure, pointed at small fields at last.

LAYER 2

The field model

Each plot gets its own running model: crop, planting date, soil class, irrigation setup, and its own multi-season history. The model judges anomalies against this field’s own record.

LAYER 3

The advisory engine

Rules and models that convert observations into ranked, dated actions: scout this corner, hold irrigation two days, expect harvest pressure early. Every advisory carries its evidence.

LAYER 4

The farmer surface

A phone-first interface in plain language, built for two-minute sessions. Optional sensor and machinery integrations extend it and are never the price of entry.

PLANNED
QUESTIONS

Asked.
Answered.

Which farms is Field Intelligence built for?

Small and family farms first. VF designs the system from Gozo outward: terraced plots, mixed crops, scarce water and no data team. It serves family farms, part-time growers, small cooperatives sharing one system across many plots, and agronomists advising small-farm portfolios. The precision-farming industry packaged its tools for estates measured in thousands of hectares; this scales the same class of analysis down.

Do I need sensors or new equipment?

No proprietary sensors are required to start. The observation layer uses Sentinel-2 satellite imagery and regional weather models, ingested per registered field boundary, which costs the farmer nothing because it is European public infrastructure. Optional sensor and machinery integrations extend the system later and are never the price of entry.

What does the system tell me?

Ranked, dated actions in plain language: scout this corner, hold irrigation two days, expect harvest pressure early. It flags crop stress from vegetation indices compared against the field’s own history, gives irrigation guidance built from weather, soil class and canopy response, and produces yield outlooks that sharpen as the season runs. Every advisory carries its evidence.

Does it work on a phone?

Yes. The farmer surface is a phone-first interface in plain language, built for two-minute sessions, so a farmer standing in a field with wet boots gets an answer worth acting on. The system answers questions; it does not create a new job in front of a dashboard. Web, iOS and Android are the target platforms.

When does Field Intelligence ship?

Field Intelligence is in build. The first phase runs live pilots on Maltese and Gozitan plots through a full growing season: field registration, satellite ingestion and the first anomaly and irrigation advisories. Multi-crop coverage, yield outlooks and the cooperative view follow, then public availability across Mediterranean EU markets. Register interest; pilot fields shape the product.

PLANNED PRICING

Flat for the farm.
Hectares don’t change the price.

Per-hectare pricing yields pennies on a three-hectare holding and feels like a tax, so the farm pays one flat figure. The basic satellite view stays free, because the market gives that away and so do we.
